title: Not Fearing the Assembly
note: He defines this as having no fear when you speak before an assembly you have judged fit to hear you.

couplets.plain: Those pure in speech, who know the range of words, know the kinds of assembly and don’t slip before an able one.
couplets.pm: Those with the purity of knowing the whole body of words know which assemblies are learned and which aren’t, and in a learned one they don’t speak wrongly out of fear. Some take the able things to be the subjects they have mastered.

links.quote: don’t slip before an able one
links.reason: Those who know their words stand firm and don’t slip before an able gathering.

links.quote: who know the range of words
links.reason: Describes speakers who know the range of words and stand before an able assembly.

couplets.plain: Those who can say what they have learned so that the learned take it in are called the learned among the learned.
couplets.pm: Those who can fearlessly say what they have learned in an assembly of the learned, so that the hearers take it in, are called by the world the best learned of all. They are the ones the world knows, so they are the ones it praises.

links.quote: say what they have learned so that the learned take it in
links.reason: Making the learned take in what you have learned earns the name of learned among the learned.

links.quote: so that the learned take it in
links.reason: Concerns those who stand up before a learned gathering and say what they have learned.

couplets.plain: Those who die among the enemy are common. Those who have no fear in an assembly are rare.
couplets.pm: Many in the world can go among enemies without fear and die there. Few can go into an assembly without fear and speak.

links.quote: Those who have no fear in an assembly are rare

couplets.plain: Say what you have learned so that the learned take it in, and from those who have learned more, take that more.
couplets.pm: Say what you have learned so that an assembly of those learned in many books takes it in, and get from those deeper in learning what goes beyond it. No one can learn everything. Where many with different learning sit, speak in a way that suits them. They will speak too, and you can hear what you never got to learn.

links.quote: from those who have learned more, take that more
Say what you have learned so that the learned take it in

couplets.plain: Learn by the right path and know the measure, so that you can answer in an assembly without fear.
couplets.pm: Ministers should study logic, which is reached by way of grammar, so that they can answer without fear what foreign rulers say in their assemblies. Logic must come after grammar, so grammar is the path. Only those learned in the forms of debate and its tricks can say the word that beats another’s, so study them without error.
couplets.note: He takes அளவு, measure, to be logic, and ஆறு, the path, to be grammar. The Tamil names neither.

links.quote: answer in an assembly without fear
links.reason: Fearless answering is the stated goal, and right learning is the training for it.

links.quote: so that you can answer in an assembly without fear
links.reason: Tells the would-be speaker to learn by the right path before facing a gathering.

links.quote: Learn by the right path and know the measure
links.reason: Tells a nervous speaker that learning by the right path is what takes the fear away.

couplets.plain: What has a sword to do with those who lack hard courage? What have books to do with those who fear a subtle assembly?
couplets.pm: What has a sword to do with those who lack hard courage? In the same way, what have books to do with those who fear an assembly of subtle minds? They have no right to books.

links.quote: those who lack hard courage
links.reason: Asks what someone without courage wants with a sword at all.

links.quote: those who fear a subtle assembly
links.reason: Books are nothing to one who fears an assembly of subtle minds.

links.quote: What has a sword to do with those

couplets.plain: The learning of a man who fears the assembly is a bright sword in a eunuch’s hand among the enemy.
couplets.pm: The books learned by a man who fears the assembly he should speak in are like the sharp sword held by a eunuch who fears the enemy she should strike. He defines a eunuch as mostly female in nature, with some male nature too. The battlefield is right and the sword is good, yet the holder’s fault makes it worthless. So too the assembly and the books.
couplets.sensitive: uses eunuchs as a byword for uselessness

links.quote: The learning of a man who fears the assembly
a bright sword in a eunuch’s hand

couplets.plain: Those who can’t speak so that a good assembly takes it in are of no use, however much they have learned.
couplets.pm: Those who, out of fear, can’t say good things in an assembly of the good in a way that suits it are of no use to the world, though they have learned many books. They don’t speak before those who could judge, so no one knows their learning is real. Some read it as: they get no fruit from their learning.

links.quote: can’t speak so that a good assembly takes it in
links.reason: Wide learning counts for nothing in one who can’t make a good assembly take in what is said.

links.quote: however much they have learned

couplets.plain: They say those who have learned and understood, yet fear an assembly of the good, are lower than the unlearned.
couplets.pm: Those who have learned books and grasped their use, yet fear an assembly of the good and don’t speak there, are called lower than the unlearned by the world. They neither gain the fruit of learning nor pass it to others, and are left with only the pain of having studied.

links.quote: fear an assembly of the good
links.reason: Fear of an assembly of the good drops the learned below even the unlearned.

links.quote: those who have learned and understood
links.reason: Speaks of those who have learning yet fear an assembly of the good.

couplets.plain: Those who fear the assembly and can’t get across what they have learned are alive, yet they are like those who are not.
couplets.pm: Those who fear the assembly and can’t say what they have learned in a way that suits it are alive, but the world doesn’t count them, so they are like the dead.

links.quote: fear the assembly and can’t get across what they have learned
are alive, yet they are like those who are not
links.reason: Still alive, those who can’t speak before others are counted among those who are not.

ideaLinks.quote: Learn by the right path and know the measure, so that you can answer in an assembly without fear
ideaLinks.reason: Learning by the right path is given as the way to answer unafraid in any assembly.
